title: LSTM and mixture-of-experts research
intro: Does learned expert routing improve prediction or simulated net performance over a comparable single model?
notice: The interactive chart below is a synthetic interface demonstration. It is not a market-data backtest or evidence of profit.
data: Existing input: 10 US stocks and SPY, 953 sessions from January 2023 to October 2026. The retained snapshot is split adjusted, excludes dividends, uses a fixed current universe and has previously been examined. Research acceptance and publication rights remain unverified.
timing: Signals use information available after the close. Hypothetical entry is the next session’s open and exit is the following open. Labels and training cutoffs follow those timestamps; class 0 means cash.
failed: Chart unavailable. The data table remains available below.
table: Synthetic values and accessible chart alternative
models: Logistic regression, a small LSTM, a parameter-matched LSTM, equal-weight experts, independent ensembles, learned dense routing and real top-2 dispatch. Transformer and routing ablations are separate experiments.
audit: Each run retains its dates, probabilities, model and scaler, router loads, costs, account marks, configuration and checksums. Repeated seeds and rolling folds remain paired; incomplete runs are labeled partial.
limitations: A successful pipeline is not a profitable strategy. Retrospective results cannot become an untouched holdout, and zero trades must be visible.
migration: This is the new home for the moe-lstm project. The original repository and historical artifacts remain available.
cmnote: Confusion matrices use ordinary accessible tables in run reports. No measured confusion counts are invented for this interface fixture.
